brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall
requirements.evidence: A flat-backed rack of 6 cells (piece 0..2,0 at levels 0 and 1), joined with snaps and joint bolts, with all its hangers on one back side.
5 hex-acc-keyhole accessories facing the same way: accessory:0#0,0#1, 0#1,0#1, 0#2,0#1, 1#0,0#1 and 1#2,0#1.

6 hex-acc-hook plates (12 hooks) on the front: accessory:0#*,0#4 and 1#*,0#4. The hooks are there, but no tool props can hang on them; the staging only accepts tape and cable coils (shown: prop:1 gaffer tape, prop:2 and prop:3 cable coils). Whether a given hand tool fits a hook, and how much weight the hooks and keyholes can hold, isn't something the configurator checks. That depends on the print material and the wall screws.

finish.summary: I built a wall rack from six hex cells in a 3-wide, 2-high block. Five keyhole hangers sit on the back faces, all facing the same way: three on the bottom row and one at each end of the top row. Six hook plates (two hooks each) sit on the front faces. I ran the house rules (solid end caps, joint bolts). check_build passes with no rule errors and meshClash reads "clear". It still notes 8 faces that could take a cap; that's information only and I left them uncapped. For the staging, the only props that can hang on these hooks are cable coils, gaffer tape or FPV goggles. So I hung gaffer tape and two cable coils on the top row. The bottom-row hooks are bare, because a prop hung there would reach the bench in the staging.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
